hardware_summary: 5x GE Frame 5 gas turbines generating site electricity plus 4x GE Frame 7EA gas turbines mechanically driving the two trains' refrigeration compressors.
source_notes: The Prigorodnoye LNG plant (Sakhalin-2, operator Sakhalin Energy) runs on-site gas turbines for both power and process drive: four GE Frame 7EA gas turbines mechanically drive the two LNG process trains' refrigeration compressors, and five GE Frame 5 gas turbines generate electricity for the site. This is a mixed site (real generator sets + mechanical drives) = mechanical:True. EVIDENCE: GE's own press release (equipment vendor primary source) on a $333M service-contract extension states: 'four GE Frame 7EA gas turbines that drive the process trains for Sakhalin's liquefied natural gas (LNG) plant and five GE Frame 5 gas turbines that are used for electricity production at the site.' nsenergybusiness.com's Sakhalin-2 project profile independently states the identical turbine allocation (4x Frame 7EA process-train drive vs 5x Frame 5 electricity generation), confirming the vendor's account from a second, independent trade-press source. Note: the Onshore Processing Facility (OPF) near Nogliki, ~800km north, has its own separate 4x25MW=100MW power plant per Sakhalin Energy's own site (sakhalinenergy.ru/en/company/assets/opf/) — that is upstream gas processing infrastructure at a DIFFERENT location from the Prigorodnoye LNG terminal (lat/lon given, 46.6288/142.9112, matches Prigorodnoye/Aniva Bay, not the OPF) and is NOT counted as this terminal's captive power. MECHANICAL-DRIVE DETAIL: 4x GE Frame 7EA gas turbines drive the LNG process trains (mechanical/shaft drive, no electricity generated) per GE's own service-contract release and corroborating trade press. A commonly circulated ~129 MW aggregate figure for the separate 5x GE Frame 5 electric generator sets could not be independently corroborated in 2 verified sources (it traces back to gem.wiki, which is banned as a citation) and is NOT reported as electric_mw. ORCHESTRATOR QC NOTE: Confirms the vendor-primary chain and records why electric_mw is deliberately blank. CITATION VERIFICATION: Orchestrator re-verified both URLs: ge.com press release PASSES 'Frame 7EA' (equipment-vendor primary source, and the origin of the 4x Frame 7EA mechanical-drive / 5x Frame 5 generator split); nsenergybusiness.com Sakhalin-2 profile PASSES 'Frame 7EA' via Wayback snapshot 20260521173001 after an HTTP 403 bot-block -- kept live per the bot-block-is-not-dead rule. electric_mw correctly left BLANK: the widely-repeated ~129 MW figure for the 5x Frame 5 generators traces back to gem.wiki and was rightly refused rather than cited circularly. hardware_summary: 16.5 MW electricity-production module built into FSRU LNG Croatia's stern, DFDE engines burning recovered boil-off gas, powering the vessel and the shore side.
source_notes: FSRU LNG Croatia has a 16.5 MW electricity-production module built into the vessel's stern during its 2020 carrier-to-FSRU conversion, generating power for both the FSRU itself and the shore side of the Krk terminal. The module runs on DFDE (dual fuel diesel electric) engines that burn boil-off gas (BOG) recovered from the cargo tanks as fuel. EVIDENCE: "isti se pomoću dvostupanjskih kompresora otprema prema modulu za proizvodnju električne energije gdje se koristi kao gorivo u DFDE (engl. dual fuel diesel electric) motorima koji služe za proizvodnju električne energije" — '[BOG] is sent via two-stage compressors to the electricity-production module, where it is used as fuel in DFDE (dual fuel diesel electric) engines that serve for electricity production.' And: "strojarnica ili modul za proizvodnju električne energije (16,5 MW)" — 'engine room or electricity-production module (16.5 MW).'. FUEL BASIS: Boil-off gas (BOG) generated from the cargo tanks is compressed via two-stage compressors and fed as fuel to DFDE (dual fuel diesel electric) engines in the onboard electricity-production module — stated explicitly by LNG Hrvatska's own engineers (Ivan Fugaš, Marko Častek) in the technical paper 'Terminal za UPP na otoku Krku – FSRU "LNG Croatia"', Nafta i Plin Vol. 42, No. 174-175 (2022), pp. 62-66. ELECTRIC MW: 16.5. PRIOR VERDICT: Prior pass had established the 16.5 MW module's existence but left FUEL TYPE as the critical open unresolved question, since diesel-only would be NO. This pass retrieved and read the full hrcak.srce.hr technical paper (live page bot-blocks direct fetch with a 418 'confirm you're not a robot' challenge, so the verified citation is a working Wayback Machine snapshot of the PDF) and found it explicitly documents DFDE engines burning BOG as fuel. Resolved to YES, green confidence. ORCHESTRATOR QC (2026-07-27): CLAIM SPLIT. lng.hr does NOT carry the 16,5 MW figure ('16,5' and 'DFDE' both FAIL there); it corroborates only the EXISTENCE of captive generation, verified on 'generates electricity for the purpose of operating the terminal'. The 16.5 MW + DFDE/BOG fuel basis cite to the hrcak.srce.hr engineers' paper (via Wayback), verified on '16,5' + 'DFDE'. Two independent origins for the Boolean -> green holds.

It is fitted with 2x Wärtsilä 12V50DF dual-fuel main engines in a diesel-electric (DFDE) arrangement — in this architecture the gas-capable main engines, not a separate mechanical shaft, generate essentially all the vessel's electric power (propulsion when underway, plus every hotel/cargo/regasification load while moored). Wärtsilä's 50DF-series engines are designed to run in gas mode (burning boil-off gas, with pilot diesel injection typically <1% of full-load fuel) as their normal/primary mode, auto-switching to diesel only if gas supply is interrupted — the standard industry pattern for LNG-carrier/FSRU dual-fuel plants. hardware_summary: Gas-turbine mechanical drive of the methane/ethane refrigerant-circuit compressors (GPA units) in Novatek's Arctic Cascade trains, per two successive supplier contracts.
source_notes: Obsky LNG's liquefaction trains are designed around gas-turbine MECHANICAL DRIVE of the on-site methane/ethane refrigerant-circuit compressors (ГПА) — captive gas power via mechanical drive, not electric-drive as hypothesized. This is confirmed across two successive equipment-supplier phases of the same terminal, both built on Novatek's own patented 'Arctic Cascade' liquefaction technology (the same technology as Yamal LNG's Train 4): (1) a March 2020 contract (~EUR130m) with Siemens + Kazankompressormash (GMS group) for 7 x Siemens SGT-700 gas turbines (32.8 MW each, one spare) as compressor drives, plus 10 Kazan-made methane/ethane-circuit compressors; (2) after Novatek moved to terminate that contract (announced ~March 2021) amid a broader equipment review, a Chinese CGT25-D 'gas-pumping' gas turbine (27 MW, industrial derivative of the naval GT-25000) was reported as the turbine to be used at Obsky LNG in Sabetta. A separate ЮМЗ turboexpander-compressor unit (20 MW) built for the current (post-2022 'Arctic Cascade Modified', 2-line/6 Mtpa) configuration is NOT gas-fired generation (it recovers pressure-drop energy within the liquefaction process) and does not itself support a captive-power finding, but it does not displace the gas-turbine-compressor-drive architecture either. EVIDENCE: Kommersant (GMS group direct quote): "Siemens поставит на две линии завода семь турбин SGT-700 (32,8 МВт, одна из турбин запасная...)... «Казанькомпрессормаш» поставит компрессоры собственного изготовления и газотурбинные установки производства компании Siemens в качестве приводов ГПА." tek-all.ru / bmpd.livejournal.com corroborate with the Chinese CGT25-D as the turbine reported for use at Obsky LNG, describing it as a "газоперекачивающая газовая турбина" (gas-pumping/mechanical-drive turbine). FUEL BASIS: Natural gas (feed gas) combustion turbines. Both reported turbines are explicitly gas-pumping/mechanical-drive gas turbines, not diesel or electric: Siemens SGT-700 (industrial gas turbine) and the Chinese CGT25-D (naval-derived industrial gas turbine, 'газоперекачивающая газовая турбина'). MECHANICAL DRIVE: 7 x Siemens SGT-700 gas turbines, 32.8 MW each (one spare), as mechanical drive for the methane/ethane refrigerant-circuit compressors — 2020 contract with Kazankompressormash/GMS. Reported successor/alternative: 1 x Chinese CGT25-D 'gas-pumping' turbine, 27 MW (industrial derivative of naval GT-25000), reported in 2021 for the same compressor-drive role after the Siemens contract was slated for termination. Current post-2022 'Arctic Cascade Modified' 2-line (3 Mtpa/line) configuration's exact final turbine supplier/count is not confirmed by a post-2022 primary source, but retains the same gas-turbine mechanical-drive architecture (Arctic Cascade template, shared with Yamal LNG Train 4's ~25 MW turbine + compressor group). PRIOR VERDICT: INSUFFICIENT (ran out of search budget, not because evidence was absent). CHANGED to YES: found detailed 2020-2021 equipment-procurement reporting (Kommersant, tek-all.ru, bmpd) showing the project's liquefaction trains use gas-turbine mechanical-drive compressors. hardware_summary: Onboard dual-fuel reciprocating generator sets on the two FSRUs, burning LNG/boil-off gas with ~2.5% MDO pilot; they were the terminal's primary supply from Sept 2022 until the shore-power connection in March 2023 and now run whenever grid supply fails.
source_notes: STAGED UNDER THE 2026-07-28 DIRECTIVE: 'if there is any turbine whatsoever that runs when grid supply fails, that counts as a yes.' This terminal's gas-fired generation is standby/backup (grid or shore power is the normal supply), which the prior pass classified STANDBY_ONLY and did NOT stage. The fuel gate still applies -- the standby set here is gas-fired, so it counts; a diesel-only emergency genset still would not. EVIDENCE: the draft environmental permit for EemsEnergy Terminal states verbatim: 'Tot de aansluiting op het elektriciteitsnet kunnen de FSRU's zelf voorzien in de elektriciteitsvoorziening. Hiervoor wordt in de fase voor elektrificatie LNG en BOG gebruikt in combinatie met een kleine hoeveelheid (2,5%) MDO (marine dieselolie) om ervoor te zorgen dat er een ontsteking plaatsvindt. Na deze aansluiting op het net zal er alleen bij stroomuitval nog sprake zijn van eigen energieopwekking.' (Until the grid connection the FSRUs could supply their own electricity, using LNG and BOG with ~2.5% MDO pilot fuel; after that connection, own generation occurs only on a power outage.) Two facts follow, either of which now carries the True: (1) the onboard dual-fuel sets were the terminal's PRIMARY power source from commissioning in Sept 2022 until shore power (walstroom) was completed around March 2023, and (2) they remain in place to run on grid failure. Gas-fired (LNG/BOG with a 2.5% MDO pilot), so the fuel gate passes. PRIOR VERDICT: STANDBY_ONLY, not staged.

The fuel gate still applies -- the standby set here is gas-fired, so it counts; a diesel-only emergency genset still would not. EVIDENCE: the project's electrical technical report states 'Il sistema di emergenza dell'impianto e garantito da un gruppo cogeneratore con potenza nominale di circa 3000 kW, funzionante a 6,6 kV, progettato per alimentare le utenze critiche ed essenziali... in caso di indisponibilita della rete principale... Il gruppo cogeneratore sara di tipo bifuel, in grado di operare sia con metano che con gasolio... Il metano sara fornito direttamente dal sistema BOG (Boil-Off Gas)... source_notes: STAGED UNDER THE 2026-07-28 DIRECTIVE: 'if there is any turbine whatsoever that runs when grid supply fails, that counts as a yes.' This terminal's gas-fired generation is standby/backup (grid or shore power is the normal supply), which the prior pass classified STANDBY_ONLY and did NOT stage. The fuel gate still applies -- the standby set here is gas-fired, so it counts; a diesel-only emergency genset still would not. EVIDENCE: the concept NRD's base-case design states 'Voor de elektriciteit wordt in de basis uitgegaan van het gebruik van walstroom uit het elektriciteitsnet... Aan boord van de FSRU bestaat daarnaast de mogelijkheid om stroom te genereren door middel van gasgeneratoren. Dit draagt bij aan de leveringszekerheid van elektriciteit' and, explicitly, 'Bij normale bedrijfsvoering zijn de generatoren van de FSRU niet in bedrijf' (under normal operation the FSRU's generators are not running). So the design pairs shore power as the base case with onboard GAS generators for supply security -- gas-fired standby, which the 2026-07-28 directive makes a True. Revisit if a later MER/permit supersedes the NRD's power basis.
